mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate over the past three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a contraction in the housing sector, which reduces consumer wealth and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline in the most recent reporting period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS and HOUST both decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 105), manufacturing sector weakness reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past three months signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point increase in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signal a monetary policy tightening cycle in response to high inflation, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized), consumer and business spending accelerates, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
